# The built-ins of cog-lisp

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from the image: do not edit by hand. -->

Only these names exist. `[x]` is optional; `x ...` is any number of them.

## Special forms

- `(begin form ...)`: Evaluates the forms in order and answers the last; at top level each is a top-level form.
- `(define name value), (define (name . params) body ...)`: Defines name, globally at top level or locally at the start of a body. A body that starts with a string keeps it as its documentation.
- `(define-macro (name . params) body ...)`: A macro that is not hygienic: its expander gets the operands and answers code, whose names mean what they mean where it is used.
- `(define-syntax name [documentation] (syntax-rules ...))`: A hygienic macro, at top level or local to a body.
- `(if test then [else])`: Evaluates then if test is true (anything but #f), else else.
- `(lambda params body ...)`: A procedure. params is (a b), (a b . rest) or rest; a body may start with internal definitions, and with a documentation string.
- `(let ((name init) ...) body ...), (let loop ((name init) ...) body ...)`: Binds each name to its init, evaluated outside the bindings; the named form also binds loop to the body as a procedure.
- `(let-syntax ((name (syntax-rules ...)) ...) body ...)`: Local macros, defined in the enclosing scope, for the body.
- `(letrec-syntax ((name (syntax-rules ...)) ...) body ...)`: Local macros that can use each other, for the body.
- `` (quasiquote template), `template ``: The template as data, with (unquote x) and (unquote-splicing x), written ,x and ,@x, filled in.
- `(quote datum), 'datum`: The datum itself, not evaluated.
- `(send receiver selector arg ...), [receiver selector arg ...]`: Sends a Smalltalk message; the selector is spelled as in Smalltalk (at:put:).
- `(set! name value), (set! (proc arg ...) value)`: Assigns value to the variable name, local or global. With a call as its target it assigns through the setter of proc, as SRFI 17 specifies: ((setter proc) arg ... value), so (set! (car x) v) sets the first element of x and (set! (vector-ref v i) x) a slot of v.
- `(smalltalk Name)`: The Smalltalk global Name, such as a class.
- `(syntax-error message form ...)`: Stops compilation with message and the forms, for a macro to report a misuse.
- `(syntax-rules [ellipsis] (literal ...) (pattern template) ...)`: The transformer of a hygienic macro: the first pattern a use matches gives its template, filled in.

## Derived forms

- `(and e ...)`: The first false value, or the last value; #t for none. Evaluation stops at the first false value.
- `(case key ((datum ...) e ...) ... (else e ...))`: The body of the first clause with a datum eqv? to key; a clause may use => proc, called with key.
- `(cond (test e ...) ... (test => proc) ... (else e ...))`: The body of the first clause whose test is true; with =>, proc called with the test value; else matches anything.
- `(do ((var init step) ...) (test result ...) body ...)`: A loop: binds each var to its init, then until test is true runs the body and steps each var; answers the results.
- `(guard (var clause ...) body ...)`: Evaluates the body; if it raises, binds var to what was raised and tries the cond clauses, raising again if none matches.
- `(let* ((name init) ...) body ...)`: As let, but each init sees the bindings before it.
- `(let*-values ((formals expr) ...) body ...)`: As let-values, but each expr sees the bindings before it.
- `(let-values ((formals expr) ...) body ...)`: Binds the values of each expr to its formals, as lambda parameters, evaluated outside the bindings.
- `(letrec ((name init) ...) body ...)`: As letrec*: bindings visible to every init and the body.
- `(letrec* ((name init) ...) body ...)`: Bindings visible to every init and the body, assigned in order: for procedures that call each other.
- `(library name (export name ...))`: The first form of a library's file: the file's top-level definitions belong to the library name, and only the names exported are brought in by (require 'name). Each definition is also reachable by its full name, name:definition, from anywhere.
- `(or e ...)`: The first true value, or #f; evaluation stops there.
- `(parameterize ((param value) ...) body ...)`: Evaluates the body with each param giving value (after its converter), and gives the old values back however the body is left: by returning, an error or a restart.
- `(restart-case form (name (param ...) body ...) ...)`: Evaluates form with named restarts; invoking one leaves form and evaluates its body with the arguments.
- `(unless test body ...)`: Evaluates the body when test is false.
- `(when test body ...)`: Evaluates the body when test is true.

## Equality and types

- `(boolean? x)`: True if x is #t or #f.
- `(char? x)`: True if x is a character.
- `(eq? a b)`: True if a and b are the same object.
- `(equal? a b)`: True if a and b are eqv?, or pairs, vectors or strings with equal? contents.
- `(eqv? a b)`: True if a and b are the same object, or numbers of the same exactness and value, or the same character.
- `(integer? x)`: True if x is an integer, exact or not: (integer? 2.0) is true.
- `(not x)`: True if x is #f, the only false value.
- `(number? x)`: True if x is a number.
- `(procedure? x)`: True if x is a procedure.
- `(string? x)`: True if x is a string.
- `(symbol? x)`: True if x is a symbol.

## Numbers

- `(* z ...)`: The product of the numbers; 1 for none.
- `(+ z ...)`: The sum of the numbers; 0 for none.
- `(- z w ...)`: z minus each w in turn; with one argument, its negation.
- `(/ z w ...)`: z divided by each w in turn; with one argument, its reciprocal. Exact division stays exact (1/3); a float divided by zero gives an infinity or NaN.
- `(< x1 x2 ...)`: True if the numbers are strictly increasing.
- `(<= x1 x2 ...)`: True if the numbers never decrease.
- `(= z1 z2 ...)`: True if the numbers are all equal.
- `(> x1 x2 ...)`: True if the numbers are strictly decreasing.
- `(>= x1 x2 ...)`: True if the numbers never increase.
- `(abs x)`: The absolute value of the real number x.
- `(acos z)`: The arccosine of z; +nan.0 outside -1 to 1.
- `(asin z)`: The arcsine of z; +nan.0 outside -1 to 1.
- `(atan y [x])`: The arctangent of y, or of y/x in the right quadrant.
- `(ceiling x)`: The smallest integer not less than x; a float stays a float.
- `(complex? x)`: True if x is a number: there are no non-real numbers built in.
- `(cos z)`: The cosine of z, in radians.
- `(denominator q)`: The denominator of the rational q in lowest terms, always positive.
- `(even? n)`: True if the integer n is even.
- `(exact z)`: The exact number equal to z: a float gives the fraction it holds exactly. An error for an infinity or NaN.
- `(exact->inexact z)`: The old name of inexact.
- `(exact-integer-sqrt n)`: Two values: the largest integer s with s*s not above n, and n - s*s.
- `(exact-integer? x)`: True if x is an exact integer.
- `(exact-rational? x)`: True if x is an exact integer or an exact fraction.
- `(exact? z)`: True if the number z is exact.
- `(exp z)`: e raised to the power z.
- `(expt z1 z2)`: z1 raised to the power z2: exact for an exact base and an exact integer power.
- `(finite? z)`: True if the number z is neither infinite nor NaN.
- `(floor x)`: The largest integer not greater than x; a float stays a float.
- `(floor-quotient n d)`: The quotient of n by d, rounded toward minus infinity.
- `(floor-remainder n d)`: The remainder of n by d after floor-quotient; it has the sign of d.
- `(floor/ n d)`: Two values: the quotient of n by d rounded toward minus infinity, and the remainder, which has the sign of d.
- `(gcd n ...)`: The greatest common divisor of the integers, never negative; 0 for none.
- `(inexact z)`: The float nearest to z.
- `(inexact->exact z)`: The old name of exact.
- `(inexact? z)`: True if the number z is inexact (a float).
- `(infinite? z)`: True if the number z is +inf.0 or -inf.0.
- `(lcm n ...)`: The least common multiple of the integers, never negative; 1 for none.
- `(log z [base])`: The natural logarithm of z, or its logarithm in base; -inf.0 at zero, +nan.0 below it.
- `(magnitude x)`: The magnitude of x: for a real number, its absolute value.
- `(max x y ...)`: The largest of the real numbers; inexact if any of them is.
- `(min x y ...)`: The smallest of the real numbers; inexact if any of them is.
- `(modulo n d)`: The old name of floor-remainder.
- `(nan? z)`: True if the number z is a NaN.
- `(negative? x)`: True if the real number x is less than zero.
- `(numerator q)`: The numerator of the rational q in lowest terms.
- `(odd? n)`: True if the integer n is odd.
- `(positive? x)`: True if the real number x is greater than zero.
- `(quotient n d)`: The old name of truncate-quotient.
- `(rational? x)`: True if x is a rational number: an exact rational, or a finite float.
- `(rationalize x y)`: The simplest rational number within y of x; inexact if either is.
- `(real? x)`: True if x is a real number.
- `(remainder n d)`: The old name of truncate-remainder.
- `(round x)`: The nearest integer to x, a half going to the even one; a float stays a float.
- `(sin z)`: The sine of z, in radians.
- `(sqrt x)`: The square root of x: exact for an exact perfect square, else inexact. An error for a negative number (complex numbers are not built in).
- `(square z)`: z times z.
- `(tan z)`: The tangent of z, in radians.
- `(truncate x)`: x with its fraction dropped, toward zero; a float stays a float.
- `(truncate-quotient n d)`: The quotient of n by d, rounded toward zero.
- `(truncate-remainder n d)`: The remainder of n by d after truncate-quotient; it has the sign of n.
- `(truncate/ n d)`: Two values: the quotient of n by d rounded toward zero, and the remainder, which has the sign of n.
- `(zero? z)`: True if z is zero, exact or inexact.

## Lists

- `(alist-delete key alist [=])`: A new alist without the entries whose key is key, compared as (= key entry-key) with = (equal? by default); alist itself is unchanged.
- `(any pred list)`: The first true value (pred element) answers, trying the elements in order, or #f if there is none: (any (lambda (n) (and (even? n) (* n n))) (list 1 2 3)) is 4.
- `(append list ... x)`: A list of the elements of each list in turn, ending in x, which is shared, not copied.
- `(append-map f list)`: The lists (f element) answers, appended in order: (apply append (map f list)) in one step.
- `(assoc key alist)`: The first pair of the association list whose car is equal? to key, or #f.
- `(assq key alist)`: The first pair of the association list whose car is eq? to key, or #f.
- `(assv key alist)`: The first pair of the association list whose car is eqv? to key, or #f.
- `(caaaar pair)`: The car of the car of the car of the car of pair.
- `(caaadr pair)`: The car of the car of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(caaar pair)`: The car of the car of the car of pair.
- `(caadar pair)`: The car of the car of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(caaddr pair)`: The car of the car of the cdr of the cdr of pair.
- `(caadr pair)`: The car of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(caar pair)`: The car of the car of pair.
- `(cadaar pair)`: The car of the cdr of the car of the car of pair.
- `(cadadr pair)`: The car of the cdr of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(cadar pair)`: The car of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(caddar pair)`: The car of the cdr of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(cadddr pair)`: The car of the cdr of the cdr of the cdr of pair: the fourth element of a list.
- `(caddr pair)`: The car of the cdr of the cdr of pair: the third element of a list.
- `(cadr pair)`: The car of the cdr of pair: the second element of a list.
- `(car pair)`: The first element of pair.
- `(cdaaar pair)`: The cdr of the car of the car of the car of pair.
- `(cdaadr pair)`: The cdr of the car of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(cdaar pair)`: The cdr of the car of the car of pair.
- `(cdadar pair)`: The cdr of the car of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(cdaddr pair)`: The cdr of the car of the cdr of the cdr of pair.
- `(cdadr pair)`: The cdr of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(cdar pair)`: The cdr of the car of pair.
- `(cddaar pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the car of the car of pair.
- `(cddadr pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the car of the cdr of pair.
- `(cddar pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(cdddar pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the cdr of the car of pair.
- `(cddddr pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the cdr of the cdr of pair.
- `(cdddr pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of the cdr of pair.
- `(cddr pair)`: The cdr of the cdr of pair: a list without its first two elements.
- `(cdr pair)`: The second element of pair: for a list, the rest of it.
- `(cons a b)`: A new pair whose car is a and whose cdr is b.
- `(delete x list [=])`: The elements of list that are not x, compared with = (equal? by default), in order.
- `(delete-duplicates list [=])`: list without its repeated elements, compared with = (equal? by default): the first of each is kept, in order.
- `(every pred list)`: #t for an empty list; otherwise #f as soon as (pred element) is false, else the value pred answered for the last element.
- `(filter pred list)`: The elements of list for which (pred element) is true, in order.
- `(filter-map f list)`: The true values of (f element), in order: map, keeping only what is not #f.
- `(find pred list)`: The first element of list for which (pred element) is true, or #f if there is none.
- `(fold kons knil list)`: Combines the elements of list from the left: (kons element accumulator), starting from knil. (fold + 0 list) sums a list; (fold cons '() list) reverses it.
- `(for-each proc list)`: Calls proc on each element of list, in order, for its effect.
- `(iota count [start [step]])`: A list of count numbers: start (0 by default), then each step (1 by default) more. (iota 5) is (0 1 2 3 4); (iota 5 1) is (1 2 3 4 5).
- `(length list)`: The number of elements of list; an error for an improper or circular list.
- `(list x ...)`: A new list of the arguments.
- `(list-ref list k)`: Element k of list, counting from 0.
- `(list-tail list k)`: The list after its first k elements, sharing its structure.
- `(list? x)`: True if x is a proper list: finite, and ending in the empty list.
- `(map proc list)`: A new list of the results of calling proc on each element of list.
- `(member x list)`: The first tail of list whose car is equal? to x, or #f.
- `(memq x list)`: The first tail of list whose car is eq? to x, or #f.
- `(memv x list)`: The first tail of list whose car is eqv? to x, or #f.
- `(null? x)`: True if x is the empty list.
- `(pair? x)`: True if x is a pair.
- `(reduce f ridentity list)`: As fold with the first element as the start: (reduce + 0 list) sums a list, and an empty list answers ridentity.
- `(remove pred list)`: The elements of list for which (pred element) is false, in order: filter with the test turned around (SRFI 1).
- `(reverse list)`: A new list of the elements of list in reverse order.
- `(set-car! pair x)`: Replaces the car of pair with x.
- `(set-cdr! pair x)`: Replaces the cdr of pair with x.
- `(sort sequence less?)`: A new list (or vector, for a vector) of the elements of sequence in order by less?, stable: equal elements keep their order. (sort (list 3 1 2) <) is (1 2 3).

## Characters

- `(char->integer char)`: The Unicode code point of char.
- `(char-alphabetic? char)`: True if char is a letter.
- `(char-ci=? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the characters are the same, ignoring case.
- `(char-downcase char)`: The lower-case form of char.
- `(char-lower-case? char)`: True if char is a lower-case letter.
- `(char-numeric? char)`: True if char is a digit.
- `(char-upcase char)`: The upper-case form of char.
- `(char-upper-case? char)`: True if char is an upper-case letter.
- `(char-whitespace? char)`: True if char is white space.
- `(char<=? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the code points never decrease.
- `(char<? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the code points are strictly increasing.
- `(char=? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the characters are all the same.
- `(char>=? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the code points never increase.
- `(char>? c1 c2 ...)`: True if the code points are strictly decreasing.
- `(digit-value char)`: The value of the digit char, or #f if it is not a digit.
- `(integer->char n)`: The character with the Unicode code point n.

## Strings

- `(list->string list)`: A new string of the characters of list.
- `(make-string k [char])`: A new string of k characters, each char (a space by default).
- `(number->string z [radix])`: The text of the number z, as write writes it, in radix.
- `(string char ...)`: A new string of the characters.
- `(string->list string [start [end]])`: A list of the characters of string.
- `(string->number string [radix])`: The number string reads as, or #f; radix is 2, 8, 10 or 16.
- `(string->symbol string)`: The symbol spelled string.
- `(string-append string ...)`: A new string of the characters of each string in turn.
- `(string-ci=? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings are the same, ignoring case.
- `(string-copy string [start [end]])`: A new string of the characters of string from start to end.
- `(string-copy! to at from [start [end]])`: Copies the characters of from, start to end, into to at index at.
- `(string-downcase string)`: A new string of string in lower case.
- `(string-fill! string char)`: Replaces every character of string with char.
- `(string-index string char)`: The index of the first char in string, or #f.
- `(string-join list [separator])`: A new string of the strings of list, with separator between them.
- `(string-length string)`: The number of characters of string.
- `(string-prefix? prefix string)`: #t if string begins with prefix.
- `(string-ref string k)`: The character of string at index k, from 0.
- `(string-search string pattern)`: The index where pattern first occurs in string, or #f.
- `(string-set! string k char)`: Replaces the character of string at index k with char.
- `(string-split string char)`: A list of the parts of string between the occurrences of char.
- `(string-suffix? suffix string)`: #t if string ends with suffix.
- `(string-trim string)`: A new string of string without the white space at either end.
- `(string-upcase string)`: A new string of string in upper case.
- `(string<=? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings never decrease, by code point.
- `(string<? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings are strictly increasing, by code point.
- `(string=? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings are all the same.
- `(string>=? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings never increase, by code point.
- `(string>? s1 s2 ...)`: True if the strings are strictly decreasing, by code point.
- `(substring string start [end])`: A new string of the characters of string from start to end.
- `(symbol->string symbol)`: A new string of the name of symbol.

## Vectors

- `(list->vector list)`: A new vector of the elements of list.
- `(make-vector k [fill])`: A new vector of k elements, each fill.
- `(subvector vector start end)`: A new vector of the elements of vector from start to end.
- `(vector x ...)`: A new vector of the arguments.
- `(vector->list vector [start [end]])`: A list of the elements of vector.
- `(vector-append vector ...)`: A new vector of the elements of each vector in turn.
- `(vector-copy vector [start [end]])`: A new vector of the elements of vector from start to end.
- `(vector-fill! vector x)`: Replaces every element of vector with x.
- `(vector-for-each proc vector)`: Calls proc on each element of vector, in order.
- `(vector-length vector)`: The number of elements of vector.
- `(vector-map proc vector)`: A new vector of the results of calling proc on each element of vector.
- `(vector-ref vector k)`: The element of vector at index k, from 0.
- `(vector-set! vector k x)`: Replaces the element of vector at index k with x.
- `(vector? x)`: True if x is a vector.

## Hash tables

- `(alist->hash-table alist [equality])`: A new hash table of the pairs of alist; the first of a repeated key wins.
- `(hash-table->alist table)`: An association list of the keys and values of table.
- `(hash-table-clear! table)`: Removes every key from table.
- `(hash-table-contains? table key)`: True if table has a value for key.
- `(hash-table-copy table)`: A new hash table with the keys and values of table.
- `(hash-table-count table)`: The number of keys in table.
- `(hash-table-delete! table key)`: Removes key and its value from table.
- `(hash-table-exists? table key)`: The old name of hash-table-contains?.
- `(hash-table-keys table)`: A list of the keys of table, in the order they were added.
- `(hash-table-ref table key [missing])`: The value of key in table; if there is none, the result of calling missing, or an error.
- `(hash-table-ref/default table key default)`: The value of key in table, or default.
- `(hash-table-set! table key value)`: Associates key with value in table.
- `(hash-table-size table)`: The old name of hash-table-count.
- `(hash-table-update! table key proc [missing])`: Replaces the value of key with the result of calling proc on it.
- `(hash-table-update!/default table key proc default)`: As hash-table-update!, with default as the value of a missing key.
- `(hash-table-values table)`: A list of the values of table, in the order of their keys.
- `(hash-table-walk table proc)`: Calls proc on each key and its value.
- `(hash-table? x)`: True if x is a hash table.
- `(make-hash-table [equality])`: A new hash table comparing keys with equality: eq?, eqv? or equal? (the default).

## Control

- `(apply proc list)`: Calls proc with the elements of list as its arguments.
- `(call-with-values producer consumer)`: Calls consumer with the values producer answers.
- `(getter-with-setter get set)`: A procedure that does what get does and whose setter is set, as SRFI 17 specifies: (set! ((getter-with-setter get set) x) v) calls (set x v). get itself is left as it is.
- `(make-parameter value [converter])`: A parameter: a procedure that answers its current value when called with no arguments. A converter is applied to value and to each value parameterize gives it.
- `(setter proc)`: The procedure (set! (proc arg ...) value) calls, as (s arg ... value): set-car! for car, set-cdr! for cdr, vector-set! for vector-ref, string-set! for string-ref, hash-table-set! for hash-table-ref and for hash-table-ref/default, and any a program adds with (set! (setter proc) s). Signals an error if proc has none. The setters of the built-in getters cannot be changed.
- `(values x ...)`: Answers its arguments as several values; one value is just itself.

## Conditions and restarts

- `(abort)`: Invokes the abort restart.
- `(compute-restarts)`: A list of the active restarts, innermost first.
- `(condition-report c)`: The text that describes the condition c, as the runner shows it.
- `(condition? x)`: True if x is a condition: anything raised or signalled.
- `(dynamic-wind before thunk after)`: Calls before, thunk and after, and calls after however thunk is left.
- `(error message irritant ...)`: Signals an error with message, and the irritants for its report.
- `(error-object-irritants e)`: The irritants of the error e, as a list.
- `(error-object-message e)`: The message of the error e.
- `(error-object? x)`: True if x is an error, as error and the system signal them.
- `(file-error? x)`: True if x is an error from opening a file.
- `(find-restart name)`: The innermost active restart named name, or #f.
- `(invoke-restart restart arg ...)`: Transfers to the active restart (or the one with that name), with the arguments.
- `(raise obj)`: Raises obj to the current handlers; a handler that returns is an error.
- `(raise-continuable obj)`: Raises obj; the value the handler returns is the value of raise-continuable.
- `(read-error? x)`: True if x is an error from reading.
- `(restart-name restart)`: The name of restart, a symbol.
- `(store-value x)`: Invokes the store-value restart with x.
- `(use-value x)`: Invokes the use-value restart with x.
- `(with-exception-handler handler thunk)`: Calls thunk with handler handling what it raises.

## Evaluation and macros

- `(coverage-merge counts ...)`: Adds up the counts of several runs (each from coverage-stop, or read back from the file COGLISP_COVERAGE_DATA names), and answers one list for coverage-report: a record for each place (file, line, column and kind), in the order first seen, its count the sum.
- `(coverage-report counts [port])`: Writes what counts (from coverage-stop) never reached, by file and line: the procedures never called and the sides of an if never taken, after a summary line. Writes to port, or the current output.
- `(coverage-start [files])`: Starts a coverage session: code compiled from now on counts each procedure entry and each side of every if, so start before loading the program. files, a list of paths, limits it to those files; by default every file but cog-lisp's own lib folder. Answers #t.
- `(coverage-stop)`: Ends the coverage session, and answers its counts: a list, in the order the code was compiled, of #(file line column kind count text). kind is procedure (an entry), true or false (a side of an if); file is the full path, or #f for a form typed at the REPL, and line and column #f where no position is known. A file loaded more than once counts once per place, its copies added up.
- `(eval form)`: Compiles and runs form at top level, and answers its value.
- `(gensym [prefix])`: A new uninterned symbol, unlike any other, for a name a macro makes up.
- `(image-build-info)`: How this image was built: an association list of its seed, the bootstrap and its fixpoint, and its version, commit and build time (version, commit, built).
- `(macroexpand form)`: form expanded until it is no longer a macro call.
- `(macroexpand-1 form)`: form expanded once, if it is a macro call; else form itself.

## Output

- `(display x [port])`: Writes x for a person: strings and characters as they are, to port or the current output.
- `(format destination control arg ...), (format control arg ...)`: Writes control with its ~ directives filled in from the arguments. destination is #f or () (answer a string; () is what nil is with cl loaded), #t (the current output) or a port; with a control string first, as SRFI 28, the answer is a string. Directives, with Common Lisp parameters and flags: ~A display, ~S write (~mincol,colinc,minpad,padcharA; @ pads on the left); ~D ~B ~O ~X and ~nR integers (~mincol,padchar,commachar,intervalD; : groups digits, @ shows the sign); ~w,dF floats; ~C a character (~@C as #\c); ~% newline, ~& fresh line, ~~ tilde (each takes a count); ~P plural (~:P the previous argument, ~@P y or ies); ~* skip, ~:* back, ~n@* go to argument n; ~{ ~} iteration (~:{ sublists, ~@{ the arguments left, ~^ leaves); ~[ ~; ~] choice (~:; default, ~:[ false and true, ~@[ when true); ~( ~) case (~:( words, ~@( first word, ~:@( upper); ~? a control string and its arguments. v as a parameter takes it from the arguments, # is the number of arguments left.
- `(newline [port])`: Writes a line break.
- `(write x [port])`: Writes x so that read reads it back: strings in quotes, characters as #\x.

## Ports

- `(char-ready? [port])`: True: a character can always be read without waiting for it here.
- `(eof-object)`: The eof object, which reading answers at the end of its input.
- `(eof-object? x)`: True if x is the eof object.
- `(get-output-string port)`: The string of what has been written to the output string port.
- `(json-read string)`: The value of the JSON text in string: an object is a hash table with string keys, an array a vector, true and false are #t and #f, and null is (), the empty list. Signals an error naming the place for text that is not JSON.
- `(json-write value [port])`: Writes value as JSON text, to port or the current output: a hash table with string keys as an object (its keys sorted), a vector as an array, a string, a real number, #t and #f, and () as null. Signals an error for anything else, such as a list or a symbol.
- `(open-input-string string)`: An input port that reads the characters of string.
- `(open-output-string)`: An output port that collects what is written to it.
- `(peek-char [port])`: The next character from port, without reading it, or the eof object.
- `(read [port])`: The next datum from port (the current input by default), or the eof object.
- `(read-char [port])`: The next character from port, or the eof object.
- `(read-line [port])`: The rest of the line from port, without its line break, or the eof object.
- `(read-string k [port])`: A string of the next k characters from port, fewer at its end, or the eof object.
- `(with-output-to-string thunk)`: Calls thunk with its output collected, and answers it as a string.
- `(write-char char [port])`: Writes char to port.
- `(write-string string [port])`: Writes the characters of string to port.

## Files

- `(call-with-input-file path proc)`: Calls proc with an input port on the file, closed afterwards.
- `(call-with-output-file path proc)`: Calls proc with an output port on the file, closed afterwards.
- `(close-input-port port)`: Closes the input port.
- `(close-output-port port)`: Closes the output port, so what was written is in its file.
- `(close-port port)`: Closes port.
- `(command-line)`: A list of the program name and its arguments, as strings.
- `(current-error-port)`: The port for error messages.
- `(current-input-port)`: The port read reads from by default.
- `(current-load-path)`: The full path of the file being loaded or run, or #f.
- `(current-output-port)`: The port display and write write to by default.
- `(delete-file path)`: Deletes the file at path.
- `(file-exists? path)`: True if there is a file at path.
- `(get-environment-variable name)`: The value of the environment variable name, a string, or #f if it is not set.
- `(imports)`: What this file, or this REPL session, has imported: a list of (name . full-name), sorted by name.
- `(open-input-file path)`: An input port reading the file at path.
- `(open-output-file path)`: An output port writing the file at path, which is replaced.
- `(require 'name [option value] ...), (require "file.lisp" [option value] ...)`: Loads a library once and brings its exported names into this file (or this REPL session): name.lisp from the first folder of (hash-table-ref *env* 'library-path) that has it, or a file named by a string, beside this file. Answers the file's full path. With no options every export comes in unqualified; 'prefix p brings them in as p followed by the name ((require 'console 'prefix 'con:) gives con:rule), 'only, 'except and 'rename '((old new) ...) choose. A library's full names (console:rule) work whether or not they are imported. (require 'cl) loads the Common Lisp names, (require 'test) the test library.
- `(require-path 'name)`: The full path of the file (require 'name) would load: name.lisp in the first folder of (hash-table-ref *env* 'library-path) that has it, or #f. Loads nothing.
- `(with-input-from-file path thunk)`: Calls thunk with the current input read from the file.
- `(with-output-to-file path thunk)`: Calls thunk with the current output written to the file.
- `(write-shared x [port])`: Writes x with a datum label for every part it shares, so the sharing reads back.

## Network

- `(http-body response)`: The response's body, a string decoded by the charset of its Content-Type (UTF-8 when it names none).
- `(http-get url [headers] [timeout])`: A GET request: (http-request 'GET url headers #f timeout).
- `(http-header response name)`: The value of the response's first header called name (in any case), or #f.
- `(http-headers response)`: The response's headers, an alist of (name . value) strings with the names in lower case, in the order the server sent them. After a redirect they are the last response's.
- `(http-request method url [headers] [body] [timeout])`: Makes an HTTP or HTTPS request and answers its response, read with http-status, http-headers, http-header and http-body. method is a symbol or string (GET, POST, ...); headers an alist of (name . value) strings; body a string, sent as UTF-8 (as text/plain; charset=utf-8 unless headers give a Content-Type), or #f; timeout in seconds, 30 by default. Redirects are followed, up to 10. A 4xx or 5xx status is a response; a failure to connect, a timeout or a rejected certificate is an error whose message starts with http:.
- `(http-response? x)`: #t if x is a response from http-request.
- `(http-status response)`: The response's status code, an integer such as 200 or 404.
- `(url-encode string)`: string percent-encoded for a URL's query or path (RFC 3986): letters, digits and - . _ ~ stay as they are, and every other byte of its UTF-8 is %XX. (string-append url "?q=" (url-encode "café au lait")) asks for café au lait.

## The system

- `(disassemble proc)`: Writes the bytecode of the procedure proc.
- `(exit [code])`: Ends the program: (exit) and (exit #t) succeed, (exit #f) fails, (exit n) exits with n.
- `(load path)`: Reads and evaluates every form of the file at path, relative to the file being loaded, and answers the full path of that file. A library file brings in every name it exports, unqualified.
- `(procedure-documentation proc)`: The documentation of proc, or #f: the call form on its first line, then what it does.
- `(procedure-source proc)`: The text proc was compiled from, or #f for a primitive.
- `(save-image)`: Saves the running image, so its definitions are there when it next starts.
- `(stack-depth)`: The number of frames on the stack, for testing that loops run in constant space.

## Smalltalk interop

- `(array->list array)`: A list of the elements of a Smalltalk collection.
- `(lisp-symbol x)`: The LISP symbol spelled as x, a Smalltalk symbol or string.
- `(list->array list)`: A Smalltalk Array of the elements of list.
- `(procedure->block proc)`: A Smalltalk block that calls proc, for Smalltalk code that wants one.
- `(smalltalk-global name)`: The Smalltalk global named name (a symbol or a string), or #f.
- `(smalltalk-nil)`: Smalltalk nil, which is not a LISP value.
- `(smalltalk-nil? x)`: True if x is Smalltalk nil.
- `(smalltalk-object? x)`: True if x is a Smalltalk object that is not also a LISP value.
- `(smalltalk-selector name)`: The Smalltalk selector spelled name.
- `(smalltalk-send receiver selector arg ...)`: Sends the message selector to receiver with the arguments, chosen at run time.
- `(smalltalk-symbol name)`: The Smalltalk symbol spelled name.

## Language server

- `(read-framed-message)`: The next message on standard input, framed as the Language Server Protocol frames it (a Content-Length header, a blank line, the text), or the eof object.
- `(write-framed-message text)`: Writes text to standard output, framed as the Language Server Protocol frames it.

## The compiler and reader

- `(bootstrap-compiler directory)`: Compiles the compiler source in directory with the running compiler, then with each new stage in turn, three times; answers the stages, for bootstrap-fixpoint? and bootstrap-differences. The last stage is left installed.
- `(bootstrap-compiler-from-seed directory entries)`: As bootstrap-compiler, with a seed compiler (its entry points) as stage 0, as the image build does.
- `(bootstrap-differences stages i j)`: The labels of the forms whose methods differ between stages i and j.
- `(bootstrap-fixpoint? stages)`: True if stages 1, 2 and 3 of a bootstrap made the same methods: the compiler compiles itself into itself.
- `(bootstrap-stage0 stages)`: What stage 0 of a bootstrap was: the symbol seed.
- `(compile-form datum [reader [context]])`: The Smalltalk CompiledMethod that runs datum, made by the compiler in use. reader is the LISP reader that read datum, so its procedures keep their text.
- `(define-number-syntax predicate parser)`: A new number syntax for the reader and string->number: a token that no built-in syntax reads and that satisfies predicate is read as (parser token).
- `(define-special-form name [documentation] translator)`: Makes name a special form of the running compiler: translator, called with the compiler's state, the form, the scope and whether the form is in tail position, answers its code. The documentation is what (documentation name) answers.
- `(documentation name)`: The documentation of what the symbol name means: a special form, a macro or a procedure; #f if it has none. Its first line is the call form.
- `(documentation-category name)`: The section of the reference of the built-ins that name belongs in, or #f.
- `(lisp-check datum [reader])`: Compiles datum as eval would, signalling the error eval would, but runs only the macro definitions in it (define-macro, define-syntax, also inside a top-level begin or a macro's expansion), so the forms after it can use them. For checking a file without running it.
- `(lisp-eval datum [reader])`: Compiles and runs datum with the compiler in use, as eval does.
- `(lisp-eval-string string)`: Reads and evaluates every datum of string in turn, so procedures keep their text; answers the last value.
- `(make-reader string)`: A reader over string: reader-next reads its datums one at a time.
- `(method-listing method)`: A fingerprint of a CompiledMethod: its header, its bytecode bytes and its literals, blocks included, to compare two compilations.
- `(opal-run method)`: Runs a CompiledMethod that compile-form made, and answers its value.
- `(read-all string)`: A list of every datum of string.
- `(read-from-string string)`: The one datum string holds; an error for none or more than one.
- `(reader-datum-start reader)`: The offset, from 0, at which the datum read last starts.
- `(reader-next reader)`: The next datum, or the eof object at the end of the text.
- `(reader-position reader)`: The offset, from 0, just after what the reader has read.
- `(reader-range-of reader list)`: The start and end offsets of the text the reader read the list from, or #f.
- `(reader-source-for reader list)`: The text the reader read the list from, or #f.
- `(special-form-names)`: The names of the special forms, sorted.

## Libraries

These exist only in a file that requires their library: `(require 'cl)`
brings in the names under cl. `cl:name` reaches one from anywhere.

### cl: `(require 'cl)`

- `(1+ x)`: Returns a number incremented by one.
- `(1- x)`: Returns a number decremented by one.
- `(aref vector index)`: The element of vector at index, as vector-ref; setf can assign it. Vectors have one dimension, so one index.
- `(atom x)`: Tests whether a value is not a pair.
- `(boundp symbol)`: True if the global environment binds symbol; an error if it is not a symbol.
- `(consp x)`: Tests whether a value is a pair.
- `(defconstant name value)`: Defines name as value, and answers name. Not enforced: name can still be redefined or set.
- `(defmacro name (param ... [&rest r]) body ...)`: Defines the macro name, as define-macro does: body builds the expansion. Answers name.
- `(defparameter name value)`: Defines the variable name as value, and answers name.
- `(defsetf access update), (defsetf access (param ...) (store) body ...)`: Gives access a setter, so (setf (access arg ...) v) works: the short form calls (update arg ... v); the long form runs the body with each param bound to its argument and store to v. Answers the name access.
- `(defun name (param ... [&rest r]) body ...)`: Defines the procedure name, as (define (name param ...) body ...) does, and answers name.
- `(defvar name [value])`: Defines the variable name, as () when no value is given, and answers name. It always assigns (Common Lisp's leaves a bound name alone).
- `(dolist (x list [result]) body ...)`: Runs body with x bound to each element of list in turn, then answers result, else ().
- `(dotimes (i n [result]) body ...)`: Runs body with i bound to 0, 1, ... up to n - 1, then answers result, else ().
- `(eighth list)`: The eighth element of list.
- `(eq a b)`: Compares values using eq? semantics.
- `(eql a b)`: Compares values using eqv? semantics.
- `(equal a b)`: Compares values structurally.
- `(evenp x)`: Tests whether an integer is even.
- `(fifth list)`: The fifth element of list.
- `(first x)`: Returns the first element of a list.
- `(flet ((name (param ...) body ...) ...) e ...)`: Local procedures, visible in the e forms but not to each other.
- `(fourth list)`: The fourth element of list.
- `(funcall f args ...)`: Calls a function with the supplied arguments.
- `(gethash key table [default])`: The value table holds for key, else default, else (). Only the value: test for a key with hash-table-contains?. setf can assign it.
- `(handler-bind ((type handler) ...) body ...)`: Runs body; a condition of a type calls its handler before anything unwinds. A handler that returns declines, and the search goes on.
- `(handler-case form (type ([var]) body ...) ...)`: The value of form; or, when it signals a condition of a clause type (error, condition, t, or a Smalltalk exception class), unwinds and answers that clause body, with var bound to the condition.
- `(ignore-errors body ...)`: The value of the body, or () when it signals an error.
- `(labels ((name (param ...) body ...) ...) e ...)`: Local procedures that can call each other and themselves, visible in the e forms.
- `(last lst)`: Returns the final cons cell of a non-empty list.
- `(listp x)`: Tests whether a value is a list.
- `(mapcar f lst)`: Maps a function over a list and returns the results.
- `(minusp x)`: Tests whether a number is negative.
- `nil`: The value ().
- `(ninth list)`: The ninth element of list.
- `(nth n lst)`: Returns the element at zero-based index n.
- `(nthcdr n lst)`: Returns the tail reached after dropping n elements.
- `(null x)`: Tests whether a value is the empty list.
- `(numberp x)`: Tests whether a value is numeric.
- `(oddp x)`: Tests whether an integer is odd.
- `(plusp x)`: Tests whether a number is positive.
- `(pop place)`: Answers the first element of the list in place, a variable, and leaves the rest of it there.
- `(prog1 first e ...)`: Evaluates first and then each e, and answers the value of first.
- `(progn e ...)`: Evaluates each e in turn and answers the last, as begin does.
- `(push x place)`: Puts x on the front of the list in place, a variable, and answers the new list.
- `(remhash key table)`: Removes key from table, and answers whether it was there.
- `(remove item list)`: list without the elements eql to item (Common Lisp's; cog-lisp's own remove takes a test, as SRFI 1's does).
- `(remove-duplicates list)`: list without its repeated elements (eql), the first of each kept.
- `(remove-if test list)`: list without the elements for which test is true.
- `(rest x)`: Returns the list after its first element.
- `(second x)`: Returns the second element of a list.
- `(setf place value ...)`: Assigns each value to its place, in turn: a variable, or a call such as (car x) or (vector-ref v i), which goes through its setter. Answers the last value.
- `(setq name value ...)`: Assigns each value to its name, in turn, and answers the last value. Each name must already be defined.
- `(seventh list)`: The seventh element of list.
- `(sixth list)`: The sixth element of list.
- `(string-capitalize string)`: string with each word capitalized and the rest of it in lower case.
- `(symbolp x)`: Tests whether a value is a symbol.
- `t`: The value #t.
- `(tenth list)`: The tenth element of list.
- `(third x)`: Returns the third element of a list.
- `(unwind-protect protected cleanup ...)`: The value of protected; the cleanup forms run after it however it ends, an error included.
- `(zerop x)`: Tests whether a number is zero.

### test: `(require 'test)`

- `(check expr expected)`: Passes when the value of expr is equal? to expected; a failure shows both.
- `(check-error expr [text])`: Passes when expr signals an error, whose message contains text when text is given.
- `(check-error-class expr class)`: Passes when expr signals an error of the Smalltalk class named class, such as LispUnboundError.
- `(check-false expr)`: Passes when expr is #f.
- `(check-true expr)`: Passes when expr is true (anything but #f).
- `(check-written expr text)`: Passes when write prints the value of expr as text.
- `(define-test name body ...)`: Registers a test; run-tests runs its body, compiled when it runs, so a test can use what an earlier test defined or loaded.
- `(eval-all source)`: Evaluates each expression in source and returns the last result.
- `(run-tests)`: Runs registered tests and exits with a status based on the results.
- `(run-tests/report)`: Runs registered tests and returns a summary report.

### pretty: `(require 'pretty)`

- `(pretty-string value [indent])`: value as a readable string: a list one element a line, a hash table as #hash( key: value, ... ) with its keys sorted, nested ones indented, the rest as display shows them (strings as write does). indent, 0 by default, is the column the value starts at.

### format-source: `(require 'format-source)`

- `(format-source text [style width])`: text, cog-lisp source, laid out: a form whose elements hold no list on one line; otherwise its head and header arguments (if's test, let's bindings, define's name) on the first line, each other argument on a line of its own one level deeper, and the closing parenthesis on its own line. Comments, strings and every other token come out exactly as they went in; only whitespace changes. Indents with tabs, or with (format-source text 'spaces 2) that many spaces a level. Text that does not read is an error naming the line.
- `format-source-headers`: A value (a list): see the library's source.
